This page shows every active MLS® listing for condos in Sardis, BC. Here is how the local sub-areas compare.
Garrison Crossing
Garrison Crossing: the former CFB Chilliwack base, now a walkable village of heritage-style homes, townhomes and condos.
Sardis East Vedder
Sardis East Vedder: established family streets east of Vedder Road close to shops, parks and Sardis Secondary.
Sardis West Vedder
Sardis West Vedder: quiet cul-de-sacs and gated adult complexes west of Vedder Road near the Vedder River trails.
Sardis South
Sardis South: newer subdivisions and townhome sites toward the Vedder River and Cultus Lake Road.
Vedder Crossing
Vedder Crossing: the commercial heart of the south side, with condos and townhomes close to the Vedder River.
Promontory
Promontory: hillside view homes and newer townhome complexes above Sardis, mostly built 1995–2020.

Sardis condos are strata lots, and the BC Strata Property Act covers them. Subjects shouldn't come off until you have the Form B, two years of strata minutes and the depreciation report, along with the bylaws about pets, rentals and age restrictions. Age bylaws get enforced in 55+ and 45+ complexes, where at least one occupant has to qualify.

Each of Lower Sardis, Rosedale, Yarrow, Greendale and Fairfield Island has land in the floodplain of both the Fraser River and the Vedder River, with protection coming from the City's dike network. Before buying, ask what the flood construction level is, what the lender and the insurer will require, and whether title carries a registered geotechnical or floodplain covenant.

Schools and transit: Chilliwack is in School District 33 (SD33), with catchments for Sardis Secondary, Chilliwack Secondary and G.W. Graham Middle-Secondary, as well as for elementary zones such as Unsworth, Watson and Vedder. Do check the exact catchment with SD33 prior to buying. Vedder Road gets BC Transit service, as do Young Road and Luckakuck Way. Route 66 is the Fraser Valley Express, which carries riders between Chilliwack and Abbotsford, and then to Carvolth Exchange in Langley.

Where are condos for sale in Sardis usually located?

Most condos in Sardis come up in Garrison Crossing, Sardis East Vedder, Sardis West Vedder, Sardis South, Vedder Crossing and Promontory. Each area has its own mix of age, lot size and price, so I recommend shortlisting two or three neighbourhoods before you book showings.
How often do these Sardis condo listings update?
Several times a day, Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's MLS® feed refreshes this page, so sold statuses, price changes and new listings reach you without a long wait.
What should I check on zoning, strata or ALR before buying a Sardis condo?

A condo is a strata lot, so the BC Strata Property Act sets the rules. Request the Form B, the depreciation report and last two years' strata minutes before subjects come off, along with the bylaws, including those on rentals, pets and age restrictions. Within 55+ and 45+ complexes, age bylaws are enforced and apply to at least one occupant.
Are any Sardis condos in the floodplain?

The Fraser and Vedder Rivers have a floodplain that takes in parts of Greendale, Yarrow, Rosedale, lower Sardis and Fairfield Island, and the City's dike network is what protects it. A property's flood construction level, the requirements of its lender and insurer, and any registered geotechnical or floodplain covenant are what you should ask about.
Which schools serve Sardis condos?

Under School District 33 (SD33), Chilliwack Secondary serves the north side. G.W. Graham and Sardis Secondary are the schools for Sardis and the south side. Catchments change, so for any specific address, check with SD33.
Is public transit available near Sardis condos?

Yes. In Chilliwack, BC Transit buses operate locally on Vedder Road and Young Road as well as Luckakuck Way, and you can get to Abbotsford and Langley on the Fraser Valley Express. Bus service is minimal or absent in rural Greendale, Columbia Valley and Ryder Lake.
